reason: Both are listed, fee-based investment managers that sponsor investment funds, including ETFs, for investors. Cohen & Steers is an active manager focused on real assets and alternative income. WisdomTree is a global asset manager that began with ETPs, and it now also holds a real-asset farmland manager (Ceres). Both serve investors and institutions, and both earn management fees on assets under management. The product mix differs: WisdomTree leans toward ETPs and digital assets, while Cohen & Steers leans toward active real-asset strategies. The overlap in fund products, investors and fee model is still enough for a direct peer.
